# Chia coverage — how much of the real world does the condition language reach?

**Generated by `npx tsx scripts/chia-coverage.ts`. Do not hand-edit.**

> **This classification is heuristic.** It matches surface patterns in the
> criterion text — it does not parse the criteria, does not attempt to write
> the rules, and has not been validated against human labels. Read the
> percentages as an order-of-magnitude sanity check on whether the condition
> language is sized right, and nothing stronger. The classifier's rules, and
> a worked example of it disagreeing with a human rule author, are below.

## Corpus

[Chia](https://github.com/WengLab-InformaticsResearch/CHIA) (Kury et al.,
*Scientific Data* 2020, CC-BY-4.0), via the `bigbio/chia` mirror on
HuggingFace. **12,060 criterion lines** across
**996 trials** (Phase IV, registered on ClinicalTrials.gov).
One line = one criterion, as the corpus authors segmented them.

## Result

| Set | Criteria | Expressible | Partially | Unmodeled |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| All | 12060 | 56.7% | 12.2% | 31.1% |
| Inclusion | 4491 | 54.5% | 9.4% | 36.1% |
| Exclusion | 7569 | 57.9% | 14.0% | 28.1% |

**56.7% of real criteria are expressible** in the closed
condition language as written, a further **12.2%** carry an
expressible core inside a sentence that also says something the language cannot
(these are the `unmodeled: true` judgement calls a rule author has to make),
and **31.1%** offer nothing to compare at all.

Inclusion and exclusion criteria fail the language in different ways:
exclusions wrap a modelable core in judgement about
1.5x
as often as inclusions do (partially: 14.0% vs
9.4%), while inclusions more often name nothing
the language can compare at all (unmodeled: 36.1% vs
28.1%).

## Method

Two pattern lists, applied to each criterion:

- **anchors** — features that give a rule something concrete to compare: a
  numeric threshold, a unit, a named lab or score, a diagnosis or medication
  reference, a named clinical condition (a bare code set such as "Pregnant or
  lactating" needs no trigger word), an explicit time window, age, sex.
- **blockers** — features no closed condition language can express:
  investigator judgement, vague qualifiers ("adequate", "clinically
  significant", "stable"), consent and logistics, open-ended lists ("such as,
  but not limited to"), intent and planning, exception clauses, prognosis, and
  "would interfere with" constructions.

Then:

| Anchors | Blockers | Class |
|---|---|---|
| none | any | unmodeled |
| ≥ 1 | none | expressible |
| ≥ 1 | ≥ 1 | partially |

Most frequent anchors: `clinical-condition` (4,905), `numeric-threshold` (2,045), `diagnosis` (1,879), `time-window` (1,115), `medication` (912).

Most frequent blockers: `consent-or-logistics` (776), `vague-qualifier` (557), `open-ended-list` (537), `intent-or-plan` (381), `investigator-judgement` (274).

## Known biases

- **It reads sentences, not meaning.** A criterion whose every word is codable
  but whose *combination* is not will be scored expressible.
- **It is optimistic relative to a rule author.** COMMANDER HF's E5, "Planned
  intermittent outpatient treatment with positive inotropic drugs administered
  intravenously", was marked `unmodeled: true` by hand — a plan is not an
  event and no extract records one — while the classifier sees "treatment
  with <drug class>" and scores it *partially*. Expect the true expressible
  share to be at or below the number above, not higher.
- **It also under-counts.** Criteria that name only a procedure, a device or a
  drug allergy — "CABG or Percutaneous Coronary Intervention", "Hypersensitivity
  to camptothecin" — are code sets in practice but match no anchor, and land in
  *unmodeled*. The two biases push in opposite directions and are not netted
  out here.
- **Segmentation is Chia's, not ours.** A line holding three clauses counts
  once.
- **Phase IV only.** Chia samples Phase IV trials; earlier-phase oncology
  protocols carry heavier eligibility text.

## Examples

### Expressible

A threshold, a code set, or a time window, and nothing else in the sentence.

- *NCT00050349 (exclusion)* — "Patients with symptomatic CNS metastases or leptomeningeal involvement"  
  anchors: clinical-condition · blockers: none
- *NCT00061308 (exclusion)* — "Pregnant or lactating."  
  anchors: clinical-condition · blockers: none
- *NCT00094861 (exclusion)* — "Metastatic disease (M1)/stage 4 NSCLC"  
  anchors: clinical-condition · blockers: none
- *NCT00122070 (exclusion)* — "Are pregnant or lactating."  
  anchors: clinical-condition · blockers: none
- *NCT00182520 (exclusion)* — "Comorbid major depressive disorder diagnosis which predates OCD diagnosis"  
  anchors: diagnosis, clinical-condition · blockers: none
- *NCT00183885 (exclusion)* — "Patients who have received prior chemotherapy for unresectable disease"  
  anchors: medication, clinical-condition · blockers: none
- *NCT00198913 (exclusion)* — "type 1 diabetic or non-diabetic"  
  anchors: clinical-condition · blockers: none
- *NCT00235170 (exclusion)* — "1. Congestive heart failure;"  
  anchors: clinical-condition · blockers: none
- *NCT00236340 (exclusion)* — "Multiple pregnancy (more than 3 fetuses)"  
  anchors: numeric-threshold, clinical-condition · blockers: none
- *NCT00250640 (inclusion)* — "Patient with primary pulmonary hypertension (i.e. Idiopathic Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension or Familial Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension) and classified as NYHA functional class III (NYHA = New York Heart Association)"  
  anchors: clinical-condition · blockers: none

### Partially expressible

A modelable core wrapped in something the language cannot say. These are where `unmodeled: true` becomes a judgement call.

- *NCT00050349 (exclusion)* — "Patients with known brain metastases, unless these metastases have been treated and/or have been stable for at least six months prior to study start. Subjects with a history of brain metastases must have a head CT with contrast to document either response o..."  
  anchors: numeric-threshold, time-window, diagnosis, clinical-condition · blockers: vague-qualifier, exception-clause
- *NCT00061308 (exclusion)* — "Women of child-bearing potential that do not practice adequate contraception."  
  anchors: sex · blockers: vague-qualifier, intent-or-plan
- *NCT00094861 (exclusion)* — "Pleural or pericardial effusion greater than 100 ml in volume as documented by appropriate imaging (positron emission tomography [PET], computed tomography [CT] scan or ultrasound). If an effusion greater than 100 ml is documented by cytology to be free fro..."  
  anchors: numeric-threshold, diagnosis, medication, clinical-condition · blockers: vague-qualifier, exception-clause
- *NCT00122070 (exclusion)* — "Have participated in any other studies involving investigational products within 30 days prior to entry into this study."  
  anchors: time-window · blockers: open-ended-list
- *NCT00182520 (exclusion)* — "Any other primary DSM-IV diagnosis; DSM-IV criteria for body dysmorphic disorder, bipolar affective disorder, schizophrenia, psychotic disorder, current alcohol/substance abuse."  
  anchors: diagnosis, clinical-condition · blockers: open-ended-list
- *NCT00183885 (exclusion)* — "Patients with any active or uncontrolled infection, including known HIV infection. (Patients with active hepatitis B will be placed on lamivudine. Patients with active hepatitis C will be eligible if liver tests qualify (5.1.9)"  
  anchors: diagnosis, clinical-condition · blockers: vague-qualifier
- *NCT00198913 (inclusion)* — "type 2 diabetic, age 18 and over, informed consent,"  
  anchors: age, clinical-condition · blockers: consent-or-logistics
- *NCT00235170 (exclusion)* — "3. Planned need for major surgery (e.g. valve surgery or resection of aortic or left ventricular aneurysm, carotid end-arterectomy, abdominal aortic aneurysm surgery etc.);"  
  anchors: clinical-condition · blockers: open-ended-list, intent-or-plan
- *NCT00250640 (exclusion)* — "Any condition that prevents participation in the study, including pregnancy and other contraindications for Ventavis treatment (as listed in the current Ventavis Summary of Product Characteristics and patient package insert)"  
  anchors: clinical-condition · blockers: open-ended-list
- *NCT00279552 (exclusion)* — "Patients who were pregnant, nursing or not able to give written informed consent were excluded."  
  anchors: clinical-condition · blockers: consent-or-logistics

### Unmodeled

Nothing to compare: consent, logistics, judgement, or a clinical state with no structured correlate.

- *NCT00050349 (exclusion)* — "Patients who have been previously treated with radioactive directed therapies"  
  anchors: none · blockers: none
- *NCT00061308 (exclusion)* — "Hypersensitivity to camptothecin or nucleoside analogues."  
  anchors: none · blockers: none
- *NCT00094861 (exclusion)* — "Shielding of any part of the esophagus during radiotherapy (including posterior spinal cord shielding)"  
  anchors: none · blockers: none
- *NCT00122070 (exclusion)* — "Had an unsatisfactory response to a previous adequate trial of quetiapine as judged by a study investigator."  
  anchors: none · blockers: investigator-judgement, vague-qualifier
- *NCT00182520 (exclusion)* — "A previous adequate trial of topiramate"  
  anchors: none · blockers: vague-qualifier
- *NCT00235170 (exclusion)* — "2. CABG or Percutaneous Coronary Intervention (PCI) procedure;"  
  anchors: none · blockers: none
- *NCT00236340 (exclusion)* — "Fetus with IUGR"  
  anchors: none · blockers: none
- *NCT00250640 (inclusion)* — "The treating physician has chosen Ventavis as a suitable long-term treatment for the patient"  
  anchors: none · blockers: vague-qualifier
- *NCT00317148 (exclusion)* — "Palpable fibroids or uterine prolapse: Grade 2 or 3."  
  anchors: none · blockers: none
- *NCT00319748 (exclusion)* — "Had/have the following prior/concurrent therapy:"  
  anchors: none · blockers: none
